name: kanban
description: Kanban's tracked Codex workflows: the Kanban-invoked solve, pr-review, pr-rereview, and pr-revise, plus the user-invoked issue, autoissue, and issue-review drafting and readiness-gate workflows.

interface.shortDescription: Kanban's solve, pr-review, pr-rereview, pr-revise, issue, autoissue, and issue-review workflows
interface.longDescription: Packages the Codex-side workflows the Kanban board invokes by name: $solve claims and implements a GitHub issue through PR creation, $pr-review and $pr-rereview run the canonical opposite-brand pull request review, and $pr-revise repairs a changes-requested pull request and hands off to a fresh canonical rereview. It also packages the drafting and readiness-gate workflows a user or the review daemon invokes directly rather than Kanban's CLI: $issue drafts exactly one verified, deduplicated issue and stops for signoff, $autoissue delegates that drafting and then immediately runs the canonical review of the created issue, and $issue-review runs the canonical opposite-agent readiness gate for one numbered issue. Each workflow preserves Kanban's existing solver, reviewer, and revision authority boundaries described in docs/agent-workflow-contract.md and docs/drafting-workflow-contract.md.
defaultPrompt: Use $solve to claim GitHub issue #123, implement it in an isolated worktree, and open a tested PR.
Use $pr-review to review pull request #38 through the canonical opposite-brand workflow.
Use $pr-rereview to rereview pull request #38 after its author pushes changes.
Use $pr-revise to address the canonical changes-requested review on PR #38.
Use $issue to find and draft one actionable issue, stopping for my signoff before creating it.
Use $autoissue to draft one issue, create it after my signoff, and immediately run its canonical review.
Use $issue-review to run the canonical opposite-agent readiness gate for issue #123.
